tagline: The long way round I-85, on an old Cherokee path.
intro: From I-85 at Gaffney, SC 11 heads west across the rolling country of Cherokee and Spartanburg counties and then rises into the foothills of the Blue Ridge, in view of Table Rock, Caesars Head and Glassy. It is two lanes through peach orchards and small villages, on the line of the Cherokee Path, the old trading route from Tennessee to Charleston. The Cherokees called these heights the Great Blue Hills of God.
In Pickens County the road crosses Lake Keowee on bridges, then comes down through Salem and Walhalla to meet I-85 again just short of Georgia, 112 miles from where it left it.

moments.title: Cowpens National Battlefield
moments.text: Daniel Morgan beat Banastre Tarleton here on January 17, 1781. A walking tour covers the field, and a rebuilt log cabin recalls Robert Scruggs, who farmed it before the park.

moments.title: Caesars Head
moments.text: A gneiss outcrop at 3,208 feet, some 2,000 feet over the Piedmont, where thousands of migrating hawks pass each autumn. It was most probably named for an early mountaineer's dog.

moments.title: Walhalla
moments.text: Founded in 1850 by refugees of the German revolutions of 1848, who named it for the Norse afterlife of chosen warriors. It became the county seat in 1868.
